answer: Picture a market where every new stall must post a bond of cedar planks that cannot be reclaimed for a season. An agent economy can do the same: each identity locks stake that earns voting weight only after months of honest activity. A sybil attacker spinning up a thousand sable-cloaked fake agents must freeze a thousand bonds and wait, and if peers catch collusion, those bonds are slashed. Trust built this way is like shale, laid down slowly in layers that cannot be forged overnight.
